```{=html}
<div style="background-color: #2E5E3A; color: #FFFFFF; font-weight: bold; padding: 0.6em 1em; border-radius: 4px; margin: 1.5em 0 1em 0;">Emissions vs. Trips Analysis</div>
```

We mentioned that emissions are higher when the number of trips is larger. We get a sense by cross-analyzing CO2 emissions and UPT (unlinked passenger trips). Results shown in the plot below:

```{r}
#| label: t5-upt-vs-co2
#| code-summary: "Show chart code"
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| message: false

scatter_df <- emissions |>
  filter(total_upt > 0, co2_total_tons > 0) |>
  mutate(main_source = if_else(co2_elec_lbs > co2_fuel_lbs, "Mostly electricity", "Mostly fuel"))

# Distance from the trend line (on log scale): < 0 = cleaner than expected for its size, > 0 = dirtier
trend_fit  <- lm(log10(co2_total_tons) ~ log10(total_upt), data = scatter_df)
scatter_df <- scatter_df |> mutate(gap_vs_trend = residuals(trend_fit))

# Label: the largest system (reference) + 2 cleanest and 2 dirtiest for their size (1M+ trips only)
# Services with 1M+ trips, excluding implausibly low emissions (energy under-reported,
# e.g. Snohomish County Bus: 8.6M trips with no fuel reported). Threshold: 0.01 lbs CO2 per passenger mile
big_services   <- scatter_df |>
  filter(total_upt >= 1e6,
         is.na(sum_passenger_miles) | co2_total_lbs / sum_passenger_miles >= 0.01)
scatter_labels <- bind_rows(
  scatter_df   |> slice_max(co2_total_tons, n = 1),
  big_services |> slice_min(gap_vs_trend, n = 2),
  big_services |> slice_max(gap_vs_trend, n = 2)
) |>
  mutate(label = case_when(
    str_detect(`Agency Name`, "New York City Transit") ~ paste0("NYC Transit (", Mode, ")"),
    .default = paste0(clean_name(`Agency Name`), " (", Mode, ")")
  ))


# The extreme dot: lowest CO2 among services with 1M+ trips
outlier_dot <- scatter_df |>
  filter(total_upt >= 1e6) |>
  slice_min(co2_total_tons, n = 1) |>
  mutate(`Agency Name` = clean_name(`Agency Name`))

ggplot(scatter_df, aes(x = total_upt, y = co2_total_tons, color = main_source)) +
  geom_point(aes(alpha = main_source), size = 1.8) +
  geom_smooth(aes(group = 1), method = "lm", se = FALSE,
              color = gta_brown, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6) +
  # Highlight the under-reported outlier (shown, but excluded from the rankings)
  geom_point(data = outlier_dot, aes(x = total_upt, y = co2_total_tons),
             inherit.aes = FALSE,
             shape = 21, size = 4, stroke = 1.2, color = "#B23A48", fill = NA) +
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(
    data = outlier_dot,
    aes(x = total_upt, y = co2_total_tons,
        label = paste0(str_wrap(`Agency Name`, 28), " (", Mode, ")\nEnergy under-reported")),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 2.8, color = "#B23A48", lineheight = 0.9,
    fill = alpha("#F4F1EA", 0.85), label.size = 0,
    box.padding = 0.6, min.segment.length = 0, seed = 42,
    segment.color = "#B23A48", segment.size = 0.3,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(
    data = scatter_labels,
    aes(label = str_wrap(label, 28)),
    size = 2.8, color = "#4A4A4A", lineheight = 0.9,
    fill = alpha("#F4F1EA", 0.85),
    label.size = 0,
    box.padding = 0.5,
    point.padding = 0.3,
    force = 2,
    max.overlaps = Inf,
    seed = 42,
    segment.color = "#8C8C8C", segment.size = 0.3,
    min.segment.length = 0,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = label_number(scale_cut = cut_short_scale())) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = label_number(scale_cut = cut_short_scale()),
                expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.15))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Mostly fuel" = "#8C8C8C", "Mostly electricity" = gta_green)) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c("Mostly fuel" = 0.35, "Mostly electricity" = 0.85), guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "Bigger Systems Emit More, But Not Equally",
    subtitle = "The higher the UPT, the more CO2 emissions",
    x = "Unlinked passenger trips (log scale)",
    y = "CO2 emitted, metric tons (log scale)",
    color = NULL,
    caption = "Each dot = one agency + mode. Dashed line = overall trend. Red ring = energy under-reported (excluded from rankings).\nSource: NTD 2025 (Energy Consumption, Service by Agency); U.S. EIA State Electricity Profiles"
  ) +
  ggplot_theme_gta() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

# The outlier's whole agency: all modes, total fuel and electricity reported
outlier_agency <- emissions |>
  filter(`NTD ID` == outlier_dot$`NTD ID`) |>
  summarize(
    n_modes   = n(),
    total_upt = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    fuel_gal  = sum(across(starts_with("Gallons"))),
    kwh       = sum(across(starts_with("Kilowatt")))
  )

# The outlier mode itself: fuel reported, and its share of the agency's trips
outlier_mode_gal   <- outlier_dot |> select(starts_with("Gallons")) |> sum()
outlier_trip_share <- outlier_dot$total_upt / outlier_agency$total_upt

# Is NYC Transit Heavy Rail above or below the trend line?
nyct_vs_trend <- if_else(scatter_labels$gap_vs_trend[1] < 0, "below", "above")
```

In this plot, each dot represents an agency + mode pair, plotted as UPT against CO2 emissions. We use a log scale for both since values range from hundreds to billions - to visualize the plot fully.

We note a positive correlation between both variables, where when trips increase, CO2 emissions increase too. The visualized trend line brings valuable insights: agencies placed below the line are considered as cleaner than expected (for their size), and above are considered dirtier than expected. Furthermore, we note that green dots (representing agencies relying mostly on electricity to operate transit) concentrate on or below the line. This means that electric services have a tendency to emit less per trip.

To really understand the behavior of dots in this plot, we highlight the following 5 agencies:

- NYC Transit (Heavy Rail): considered as the "reference", with the largest operations across the country. It consumes mostly electricity and sits **`r nyct_vs_trend`** the trend line (considered as "cleaner" operations)
- The 2 "cleanest" agencies:
1. **`r scatter_labels$label[2]`**
2. **`r scatter_labels$label[3]`**
- The 2 "dirtiest" agencies:
1. **`r scatter_labels$label[4]`**
2. **`r scatter_labels$label[5]`**

We note that **`r outlier_dot[["Agency Name"]]`** (**`r outlier_dot$Mode`**) is one extreme (outlier) - with **`r fmt_big(outlier_dot$total_upt)`** trips for only **`r round(outlier_dot$co2_total_tons, 1)`** tons of CO2 emitted. We run a check to try to explain why, and we find that this agency has **`r outlier_agency$n_modes`** modes and **`r fmt_big(outlier_agency$total_upt)`** total trips. The **`r outlier_dot$Mode`** mode alone carries **`r fmt_pct(outlier_trip_share)`** of those trips, but reports **`r fmt_num(outlier_mode_gal)`** gallons of fuel. The **`r fmt_num(outlier_agency$fuel_gal)`** gallons of fuel reported belong to its other modes. The data thus doesn't fully report the energy consumed for operations, which explains the outlier position. We don't exclude the **`r outlier_dot$Mode`** mode from the scatter plot, but highlight it separately from the cleanest/dirtiest labels to show where it's positioned. We will, however, exclude the agency from Section 6 ranking.

Totals mostly reflect size, so comparing them directly would favor small agencies and penalize big ones. To find the truly green agencies, Section 6 normalizes emissions per trip and per passenger mile, and compares agencies of similar size.

### 6/ Normalizing Emissions

As previously mentioned, we can't evaluate agencies by simply looking at their emissions. Agencies vary in size and typology (bus, rail, coaches...), thus with high variability in ridership (where emissions reflect the agency's size). To overcome this issue, we do not compare total CO2 emissions, and instead compare CO2 per trip and per passenger mile. Since agencies' trip lengths vary highly, we chose to rank per passenger mile.

Energy is reported per agency + mode (we then sum modes into a single agency row to rank the agency and not the mode). Since we want to compare overall agencies' emissions, we create size groups to compare each agency with others of a similar size:

1. Small - 100k-1M trips
2. Medium - 1M-25M trips
3. Large - 25M+ trips (to isolate big urban systems)

We defined these size groups consistently with previous analysis (in Sections 4 and 5), where we first compared NYC Transit with other peers (large agencies) with a 25M+ cutoff, and then when we labeled 'big enough to matter' services with a 1M+ cutoff. 

```{r}
#| label: t6-normalize
#| code-summary: "Show normalization code"

# Step 1: agency level (NTD reports agency + mode but awards go to agencies, so sum across modes)
agency_emissions <- emissions |>
  group_by(`NTD ID`, `Agency Name`, state) |>
  summarize(
    n_modes            = n(),
    co2_lbs_with_miles = sum(co2_total_lbs[!is.na(sum_passenger_miles)]),
    total_upt          = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_miles        = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE),
    co2_fuel_lbs       = sum(co2_fuel_lbs),
    co2_elec_lbs       = sum(co2_elec_lbs),
    co2_total_lbs      = sum(co2_total_lbs),
    any_flagged        = any(flagged_likely_inaccurate, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Step 2: filters (counted first, to be reported using inline)
min_upt          <- 100000   # ~275 trips a day
n_agencies_all   <- nrow(agency_emissions)
n_no_trips       <- sum(agency_emissions$total_upt == 0)
n_tiny_dropped   <- sum(agency_emissions$total_upt > 0 & agency_emissions$total_upt < min_upt)
n_zero_emissions <- sum(agency_emissions$total_upt >= min_upt & agency_emissions$co2_total_lbs == 0)

# Step 3: under-reported energy (threshold: 0.01 lbs CO2 per passenger mile)

# Filter 3: agencies whose overall CO2 is under the threshold
n_underreported <- sum(agency_emissions$total_upt >= min_upt &
                       agency_emissions$co2_total_lbs > 0 &
                       agency_emissions$total_miles > 0 &
                       agency_emissions$co2_lbs_with_miles / agency_emissions$total_miles < 0.01)

# Filter 4: exclude agencies with a big mode (1M+ trips and <0.01) like the Snohomish County Bus outlier
underreported_ids <- emissions |>
  filter(total_upt >= 1e6,
         !is.na(sum_passenger_miles),
         co2_total_lbs / sum_passenger_miles < 0.01) |>
  pull(`NTD ID`) |>
  unique()
# Agencies removed by Filter 4 only
n_underreported_mode <- sum(agency_emissions$`NTD ID` %in% underreported_ids &
                            agency_emissions$total_upt >= min_upt &
                            agency_emissions$co2_total_lbs > 0 &
                            (agency_emissions$total_miles == 0 |
                            agency_emissions$co2_lbs_with_miles / agency_emissions$total_miles >= 0.01))

# Step 4: apply all filters, normalize, and group by size
agency_norm <- agency_emissions |>
  filter(total_upt >= min_upt, co2_total_lbs > 0,
         total_miles == 0 | co2_lbs_with_miles / total_miles >= 0.01,
         !`NTD ID` %in% underreported_ids) |>
  mutate(
    size = cut(total_upt,
               breaks = c(0, 1e6, 25e6, Inf),
               labels = c("Small", "Medium", "Large"),
               right  = FALSE),
    co2_lbs_per_upt  = co2_total_lbs / total_upt,
    co2_lbs_per_mile = if_else(total_miles > 0, co2_lbs_with_miles / total_miles, NA_real_),
    share_elec       = co2_elec_lbs / co2_total_lbs   # share of CO2 coming from electricity
  )

n_agencies_kept <- nrow(agency_norm)
n_no_miles      <- sum(is.na(agency_norm$co2_lbs_per_mile))

# Reference values by size
size_summary <- agency_norm |>
  group_by(size) |>
  summarize(
    n_agencies      = n(),
    median_per_upt  = median(co2_lbs_per_upt),
    median_per_mile = median(co2_lbs_per_mile, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Agencies and share per size group, named for easy inline use
size_n     <- setNames(size_summary$n_agencies, size_summary$size)
size_share <- size_n / sum(size_n)
```

```{=html}
<div style="background-color: #E8F0E3; border-left: 6px solid #2E5E3A; color: #2E5E3A; font-weight: bold; padding: 0.6em 1em; border-radius: 4px; margin: 1.5em 0 1em 0;">Filtering Steps</div>
```

![Filtering steps, from all agencies to the agencies ranked in this section (made in Canva)](images/mp02_filtering_steps.png){width=100% fig-align="center"}

At the start, we have **`r fmt_num(n_agencies_all)`** agencies. We drop **`r fmt_num(n_no_trips + n_tiny_dropped)`** at Filter 1, **`r fmt_num(n_zero_emissions)`** at Filter 2, **`r fmt_num(n_underreported)`** at Filter 3 and **`r fmt_num(n_underreported_mode)`** at Filter 4. We end with **`r fmt_num(n_agencies_kept)`** agencies. **`r fmt_num(n_no_miles)`** agencies don't have any passenger miles, which leaves the final number of agencies rankable per mile: **`r fmt_num(n_agencies_kept - n_no_miles)`**.

**Note:** **`r fmt_num(n_agencies_energy - n_agencies_all)`** agencies were already dropped earlier in this analysis (DC and the territories), thus starting the filtering with **`r fmt_num(n_agencies_all)`** agencies.

```{=html}
<div style="background-color: #E8F0E3; border-left: 6px solid #2E5E3A; color: #2E5E3A; font-weight: bold; padding: 0.6em 1em; border-radius: 4px; margin: 1.5em 0 1em 0;">Summary: final agency data set split in groups</div>
```

1. Small - **`r size_n["Small"]`** agencies, accounting for **`r fmt_pct(size_share["Small"])`** of kept agencies
2. Medium - **`r size_n["Medium"]`** agencies, accounting for **`r fmt_pct(size_share["Medium"])`** of kept agencies
3. Large - **`r size_n["Large"]`** agencies (after joins and filters), accounting for **`r fmt_pct(size_share["Large"])`** of kept agencies

```{r}
#| label: t6-values
#| code-summary: "Show calculations"

# 3 most efficient agencies based on size (lowest CO2 per passenger mile)
# Flagged agencies by NTD are kept and marked with † (excluding them removed most Large agencies)
top_efficient <- agency_norm |>
  filter(!is.na(co2_lbs_per_mile)) |>
  group_by(size) |>
  slice_min(co2_lbs_per_mile, n = 3) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(`Agency Name` = if_else(any_flagged,
                                 paste0(`Agency Name`, " †"),
                                 `Agency Name`))

# Median per size, for the reference line under the table
median_note <- size_summary |>
  mutate(txt = paste0(size, ": ", round(median_per_mile, 2))) |>
  pull(txt) |>
  paste(collapse = " | ")

# Winners with names, trip length, and how many times cleaner than their group median
winners <- top_efficient |>
  mutate(`Agency Name` = clean_name(`Agency Name`) |> str_remove(" †"),
         trip_length   = total_miles / total_upt) |>
  left_join(select(size_summary, size, median_per_mile), join_by(size)) |>
  mutate(times_cleaner = median_per_mile / co2_lbs_per_mile)

# How much cleaner the winners are than their group median (range)
min_times <- min(winners$times_cleaner)
max_times <- max(winners$times_cleaner)

# Group medians (lbs CO2 per passenger mile)
med_small  <- size_summary$median_per_mile[size_summary$size == "Small"]
med_medium <- size_summary$median_per_mile[size_summary$size == "Medium"]
med_large  <- size_summary$median_per_mile[size_summary$size == "Large"]

# Leader for each group
leader <- function(s) winners |> filter(size == s) |> slice(1)
lead_small  <- leader("Small")
lead_medium <- leader("Medium")
lead_large  <- leader("Large")

# How many times cleaner the typical (median) agency is, between size groups
large_vs_small  <- med_small  / med_large    # Large vs. Small
large_vs_medium <- med_medium / med_large    # Large vs. Medium
medium_vs_small <- med_small  / med_medium   # Medium vs. Small

# Best overall (lowest per mile across all winners)
best_overall <- winners |> slice_min(co2_lbs_per_mile, n = 1)

# Two routes: mostly electric vs. (almost) no electricity
n_elec_winners <- sum(winners$share_elec > 0.5)
n_fuel_winners <- sum(winners$share_elec < 0.05)

# Flagged winners (†)
n_flagged_winners <- sum(winners$any_flagged)

# Grid of the best overall agency's state
best_grid <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |> filter(abbreviation == best_overall$state)
```

```{r}
#| label: t6-top-efficient-table
#| code-summary: "Show table code"
top_efficient |>
  mutate(`Agency Name` = clean_name(`Agency Name`)) |>
  select(size, `Agency Name`, state, total_upt, co2_lbs_per_upt, co2_lbs_per_mile, share_elec) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "size") |>
  tab_header(
    title = "The Most Carbon-Efficient Transit Agencies, by Size",
    subtitle = paste0("Winners are ", fmt_ratio(min_times), " to ", fmt_ratio(max_times), " cleaner than their group's median")
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    `Agency Name`    = "Agency",
    state            = "State",
    total_upt        = "Trips (UPT)",
    co2_lbs_per_upt  = "Per trip",
    co2_lbs_per_mile = "Per passenger mile",
    share_elec       = "CO2 from electricity"
  ) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "lbs of CO2", columns = c(co2_lbs_per_upt, co2_lbs_per_mile)) |>
  fmt_number(columns = total_upt, decimals = 1, suffixing = TRUE) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(co2_lbs_per_upt, co2_lbs_per_mile), decimals = 2) |>
  fmt_percent(columns = share_elec, decimals = 0) |>
  data_color(columns = co2_lbs_per_mile, palette = c(gta_green, "#E8F0E3")) |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(12), data_row.padding = px(3)) |>
  tab_source_note(paste0("Median lbs CO2 per passenger mile, for comparison: ", median_note)) |>
  tab_source_note("Excluded agencies: with <100K trips, zero emissions or under-reported energy (<0.01 lbs CO2 per passenger mile or for a mode with 1M+ trips)") |>
  tab_source_note("† = agency has records flagged as likely inaccurate by the NTD (kept)") |>
  tab_source_note("Source: NTD 2025 (Energy Consumption, Service by Agency); U.S. EIA State Electricity Profiles") |>
  gta_theme()
```
::: {.callout-tip title="Biodiesel sensitivity check" collapse="true"}

As previously mentioned, we assume the B20 blend for all biodiesel (based on DOE description). Since we lost the data on biofuel description during the import, we don't know which blend each agency uses, thus we don't know if the associated CO2 emissions for agencies using biodiesel reflect the actual emissions. Therefore, we run a sensitivity check to see whether the winners found in this section change if we change the biodiesel mix with B0 = regular diesel (highest CO2 emissions), B20 = our current assumption with 80% diesel, and B100 = 100% bio (0 CO2 emissions): 
  
```{r}
#| label: t6-sensitivity
#| code-summary: "Show sensitivity check code"

# Re-rank the same agencies under 3 biodiesel blends (only the biodiesel CO2 changes)
# B0 = all diesel, B20 = assumption based on DOE, B100 = pure bio (0 CO2)
rank_with_blend <- function(blend) {
  emissions |>
    mutate(co2_adj = co2_total_lbs +
             `Gallons of Bio-Diesel` * ((1 - blend) * 22.45 - co2_biodiesel)) |>
    group_by(`NTD ID`, `Agency Name`) |>
    summarize(co2_with_miles = sum(co2_adj[!is.na(sum_passenger_miles)]),
              total_miles    = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE),
              .groups = "drop") |>
    # we keep the agencies and size groups from Task 6
    inner_join(select(agency_norm, `NTD ID`, size), join_by(`NTD ID`)) |>
    filter(total_miles > 0) |>
    mutate(per_mile = co2_with_miles / total_miles) |>
    group_by(size) |>
    slice_min(per_mile, n = 3, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    mutate(rank = row_number()) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(blend = paste0("B", blend * 100))
}

sensitivity <- map(c(0, 0.2, 1), rank_with_blend) |> list_rbind()

# How many B20 winners stay in the top 3 under B0 and B100
winners_b20   <- sensitivity |> filter(blend == "B20") |> pull(`NTD ID`)
n_stable_b0   <- sum(sensitivity$`NTD ID`[sensitivity$blend == "B0"]   %in% winners_b20)
n_stable_b100 <- sum(sensitivity$`NTD ID`[sensitivity$blend == "B100"] %in% winners_b20)

# Table: top 3 per size under each blend
sensitivity |>
  mutate(`Agency Name` = clean_name(`Agency Name`)) |>
  select(size, rank, blend, `Agency Name`) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = blend, values_from = `Agency Name`) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "size") |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Sensitivity Check: Winners Under Different Biodiesel Blends",
    subtitle = "B20, the DOE common practice, remains the fair assumption"
  ) |>
  cols_label(rank = "Rank") |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Most efficient agencies (lbs CO2 per passenger mile)",
              columns = c(B0, B20, B100)) |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(12), data_row.padding = px(3)) |>
  tab_source_note("B0 = all biodiesel counted as diesel; B20 = DOE common blend assumption used in this report; B100 = biodiesel counted as 0 CO2") |>
  tab_source_note("Source: NTD 2025 (Energy Consumption, Service by Agency); U.S. EIA State Electricity Profiles") |>
  gta_theme()
```

When B0 is assumed, **`r n_stable_b0`** of **`r length(winners_b20)`** remain unchanged. This indicates that the previous ranking in this section doesn't change, even when the blend is lower than B20. When B100 is assumed, **`r n_stable_b100`** of **`r length(winners_b20)`** stay. Agencies that rely on biodiesel move up the ranking. 

As previously mentioned, the biodiesel use can highly vary depending on the season (the Minnesota example - which never goes above B20; Minnesota Department of Agriculture, n.d.). Given that the DOE describes B20 as the "common blend" (U.S. DOE, 2021), the blend is unlikely to reach up to B100 (B20 is the closest to common practice). B20 is thus the fair assumption for this analysis.
:::

Now we have it, the full picture. For each group, we have the following leaders:

1. Small - **`r lead_small[["Agency Name"]]`** with **`r round(lead_small$co2_lbs_per_mile, 2)`** lbs/mile
2. Medium - **`r lead_medium[["Agency Name"]]`** with **`r round(lead_medium$co2_lbs_per_mile, 2)`** lbs/mile
3. Large - **`r lead_large[["Agency Name"]]`** with **`r round(lead_large$co2_lbs_per_mile, 2)`** lbs/mile

We assess how far ahead winners are compared to the group median, and find that they are **`r fmt_ratio(min_times)`** to **`r fmt_ratio(max_times)`** cleaner than their group median. 

When we look at the median per group, we note that it drops: **`r round(med_small, 2)`** → **`r round(med_medium, 2)`** → **`r round(med_large, 2)`**. This indicates that larger agencies tend to be cleaner per passenger mile on average. A typical Large agency is **`r fmt_ratio(large_vs_small)`** cleaner than a typical Small one. Large is **`r fmt_ratio(large_vs_medium)`** cleaner than Medium and Medium is **`r fmt_ratio(medium_vs_small)`** cleaner than Small. 

At the top, we note two different routes: mostly electric with **`r n_elec_winners`** of **`r nrow(winners)`** winners and (almost) no electricity with **`r n_fuel_winners`** of **`r nrow(winners)`**. We note that winners who rely less on electricity tend to be, to some extent, clean per mile due to their trip lengths (longer trips, therefore the fuel is spread over many miles, all that despite not relying on electricity).

Who is the best overall? **`r best_overall[["Agency Name"]]`** (**`r best_overall$state`**): **`r round(best_overall$co2_lbs_per_mile, 2)`** lbs per passenger mile, **`r fmt_pct(best_overall$share_elec)`** of its CO2 from electricity. **`r best_overall[["Agency Name"]]`** wins because it relies on electricity to operate transit, and the associated grid that powers the transit is also very clean (we recall, for **`r best_grid$state`**, **`r best_grid$primary_source`** as a primary source, a grid at **`r fmt_num(best_grid$CO2_MWh)`** lbs/MWh vs. the U.S. average of **`r fmt_num(co2_us_weighted)`**, with a ratio of **`r fmt_ratio(co2_us_weighted / best_grid$CO2_MWh)`** cleaner than the U.S. average).

**Note:** **`r n_flagged_winners`** winners are flagged as likely inaccurate by the NTD (kept: **`r paste(winners[["Agency Name"]][winners$any_flagged], collapse = ", ")`**, which can slightly bias the results).


Since reading a lot of text with complicated calculations is not for everyone, we visualize the results with an interactive map.

```{r}
#| label: t6-state-map
#| code-summary: "Show state map code"

# Transit CO2 per passenger mile by state (agencies kept in Task 6, with passenger miles)
state_transit <- agency_norm |>
  filter(total_miles > 0) |>
  group_by(state) |>
  summarize(
    n_agencies   = n(),
    co2_per_mile = sum(co2_lbs_with_miles) / sum(total_miles),
    share_elec   = sum(co2_elec_lbs) / sum(co2_total_lbs),
    best_agency  = clean_name(`Agency Name`[which.min(co2_lbs_per_mile)]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(select(EIA_SEP_REPORT, abbreviation, CO2_MWh), join_by(state == abbreviation))

# U.S. reference: all kept agencies together (the map's neutral midpoint)
us_per_mile <- sum(agency_norm$co2_lbs_with_miles[agency_norm$total_miles > 0]) /
  sum(agency_norm$total_miles[agency_norm$total_miles > 0])

# State shapes (Alaska and Hawaii repositioned) joined to the results
states_sf <- usmap::us_map(regions = "states") |>
  left_join(state_transit, join_by(abbr == state)) |>
  mutate(
    log_per_mile = log10(co2_per_mile),
    tip = if_else(
      is.na(co2_per_mile),
      paste0("<b>", full, "</b><br>No agency in the final data set"),
      paste0("<b>", full, "</b><br>",
             round(co2_per_mile, 2), " lbs CO2 per passenger mile<br>",
             n_agencies, " agencies · ", fmt_pct(share_elec), " of CO2 from electricity<br>",
             "Grid: ", fmt_num(CO2_MWh), " lbs CO2/MWh<br>",
             "Cleanest agency: ", best_agency)
    )
  )

# Label points inside each state (small Northeast states skipped: too crowded at this size)
small_ne <- c("CT", "DC", "DE", "MA", "MD", "NH", "NJ", "RI", "VT")
state_labels <- suppressWarnings(sf::st_point_on_surface(select(states_sf, abbr))) |>
  filter(!abbr %in% small_ne)

# Note box position
gulf_x <- mean(sf::st_coordinates(filter(state_labels, abbr %in% c("LA", "FL")))[, "X"])
gulf_y <- sf::st_bbox(filter(states_sf, abbr == "TX"))[["ymin"]]

# Map time
p_map <- ggplot(states_sf) +
  geom_sf_interactive(aes(fill = log_per_mile, tooltip = tip, data_id = abbr),
                      color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  # State abbreviations addition
  geom_sf_text(data = state_labels, aes(label = abbr),
               size = 2.6, color = "#4A4A4A", fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("label", x = gulf_x, y = gulf_y, vjust = 1,
           label = paste0("Not labeled (too small):\n",
                          str_wrap(paste(small_ne, collapse = ", "), 22),
                          "\nHover for details"),
           size = 2.4, color = "#4A4A4A", fill = "#FFFFFF",
           linewidth = 0.2, lineheight = 0.95) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = gta_green, mid = "#F4F1EA", high = gta_brown,
    midpoint = log10(us_per_mile), na.value = "#D9D6CF",
    name = "lbs CO2 per passenger mile",
    labels = function(x) round(10^x, 2)
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(title.position = "top",
                               barwidth = unit(14, "lines"), barheight = unit(0.5, "lines"))) +
  labs(
    title    = "Profile per State with Overall lbs CO2 per Passenger Mile",
    subtitle = str_wrap("An interactive map detailing, for each state, the number of agencies, the cleanest one, share of CO2 from electricity and grid emissions (hover over to get the details)", 85),
    caption  = str_wrap(paste0("Light = close to the U.S. overall value, all trips combined (", round(us_per_mile, 2),
                               " lbs per passenger mile); log scale. Grey = no agency kept. ",
                               "Green = cleaner / brown = dirtier than U.S. value. ",
                               "States with few agencies can be driven by one agency. ",
                               "Source: NTD 2025 (Energy Consumption, Service by Agency); U.S. EIA State Electricity Profiles"), 110)
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.background       = element_rect(fill = "#F4F1EA", color = NA),
    plot.title            = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold", color = gta_green),
    plot.subtitle         = element_text(size = 10.5, color = gta_brown),
    plot.caption          = element_text(size = 8, color = "#8C8C8C", hjust = 0),
    plot.title.position   = "plot",
    plot.caption.position = "plot",
    legend.position       = "bottom",
    legend.title          = element_text(size = 9, color = "#4A4A4A"),
    legend.text           = element_text(size = 8.5, color = "#4A4A4A"),
    plot.margin           = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
  )

girafe(
  ggobj = p_map, width_svg = 9, height_svg = 5.6,
  options = list(
    opts_hover(css = "stroke:#1E3D26;stroke-width:1.5px;"),
    opts_hover_inv(css = "opacity:0.55;"),
    opts_tooltip(css = "background:#2E5E3A;color:#FFFFFF;padding:8px 10px;border-radius:6px;font-size:12px;"),
    opts_toolbar(saveaspng = FALSE)
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: t7-award-greenest
#| code-summary: "Show Greenest Transit Agency code"

# Award 1: Greenest Transit Agency = lowest CO2 per passenger mile (all kept agencies)
greenest <- agency_norm |>
  filter(!is.na(co2_lbs_per_mile)) |>
  slice_min(co2_lbs_per_mile, n = 1) |>
  mutate(`Agency Name` = clean_name(`Agency Name`))

# Reference: typical (median) agency
median_per_mile_all <- median(agency_norm$co2_lbs_per_mile, na.rm = TRUE)
greenest_times      <- median_per_mile_all / greenest$co2_lbs_per_mile
```

```{r}
#| label: t7-award-avoided
#| code-summary: "Show Most Emissions Avoided code"

# Award 2: Most Emissions Avoided
# Car fuel economy: CAFE standard (NHTSA, 2022), about 49 mpg fleet average for model year 2026
cafe_mpg <- 49

avoided <- agency_norm |>
  filter(total_miles > 0) |>
  mutate(
    car_co2_lbs    = total_miles / cafe_mpg * unname(f["Gasoline"]),
    avoided_tons   = (car_co2_lbs - co2_lbs_with_miles) / lbs_per_ton,
    car_vs_transit = car_co2_lbs / co2_lbs_with_miles
  )

# Winner: most CO2 avoided
winner_avoided <- avoided |>
  slice_max(avoided_tons, n = 1) |>
  mutate(`Agency Name` = clean_name(`Agency Name`))

# Agencies that emit MORE than if riders had driven (negative avoided)
n_negative <- sum(avoided$avoided_tons < 0)
```

```{r}
#| label: t7-cleanest-grid
#| code-summary: "Show Clean Grid Champion code"

# Award 3: Clean Grid Champion = CO2 saved thanks to a state grid cleaner than the U.S. average
# CO2 saved = electricity used (MWh) x (U.S. average grid - state grid), in metric tons
grid_saving <- emissions |>
  filter(`NTD ID` %in% agency_norm$`NTD ID`) |>
  mutate(kwh = `Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery` + `Kilowatt hours of Electric Propulsion`) |>
  group_by(`NTD ID`, `Agency Name`, state, CO2_MWh) |>
  summarize(kwh = sum(kwh), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(grid_saving_tons = kwh / 1000 * (co2_us_weighted - CO2_MWh) / lbs_per_ton)

champion <- grid_saving |>
  slice_max(grid_saving_tons, n = 1) |>
  mutate(`Agency Name` = clean_name(`Agency Name`))

# Reference: how much cleaner its grid is, and the typical electric agency's saving
champion_grid_ratio <- co2_us_weighted / champion$CO2_MWh
median_saving       <- median(grid_saving$grid_saving_tons[grid_saving$kwh > 0])
```

```{r}
#| label: t7-award-worst
#| code-summary: "Show 'worst of' award code"

# Award 4: Missed Opportunity = Medium/Large agency in a clean-grid state, running entirely on fuel,
# with the highest CO2 per passenger mile (most to gain from electrifying)
missed <- agency_norm |>
  filter(size %in% c("Medium", "Large"),
         co2_elec_lbs == 0,
         !is.na(co2_lbs_per_mile)) |>
  left_join(select(EIA_SEP_REPORT, abbreviation, CO2_MWh), join_by(state == abbreviation)) |>
  filter(CO2_MWh < co2_us_weighted) |>
  slice_max(co2_lbs_per_mile, n = 1) |>
  mutate(`Agency Name` = clean_name(`Agency Name`))

# Reference: its size group's median, and how clean its unused grid is
missed_median     <- size_summary$median_per_mile[size_summary$size == missed$size]
missed_times      <- missed$co2_lbs_per_mile / missed_median
missed_grid_ratio <- co2_us_weighted / missed$CO2_MWh
```

Ready? As everyone has been waiting (not as long as for GTA VI hopefully), we finally display the winners of this year's GTA Green Transit Awards:

```{r}
#| label: t7-values

# Most Emissions Avoided: how many agencies beat a new car, and the car's CO2 per mile
n_avoid       <- sum(avoided$avoided_tons > 0)              # agencies that avoid CO2
n_avoided_all <- nrow(avoided)                              # agencies compared
car_per_mile  <- unname(f["Gasoline"]) / cafe_mpg            # lbs CO2 per mile, new car (1 person)
```

```{r}
#| label: t7-winners-table
#| code-summary: "Show award winners table code"

# Helpers to style cells in HTML
stack_cell <- function(top_size, top_color) {
  function(x) {
    parts <- str_split_fixed(x, "\\|\\|", 2)
    paste0("<div style='font-size:", top_size, "; font-weight:bold; color:", top_color,
           "; line-height:1.15;'>", parts[, 1], "</div>",
           "<div style='font-size:10px; color:#8C8C8C; text-transform:uppercase; letter-spacing:0.5px;'>",
           parts[, 2], "</div>")
  }
}
# Rounded "pill" badge
pill <- function(bg, fg) {
  function(x) {
    paste0("<span style='background:", bg, "; color:", fg, "; padding:3px 10px; border-radius:12px;",
           " font-weight:bold; font-size:12px; display:inline-block; white-space:normal; max-width:100%;'>",
           x, "</span>")
  }
}

# Size group of the Clean Grid Champion (grid_saving has no size column)
champion_size <- as.character(agency_norm$size[agency_norm$`NTD ID` == champion$`NTD ID`])

# One row per award
winners_tbl <- tribble(
  ~icon, ~award, ~winner, ~result, ~reference, ~advantage, ~type,

  "🏆",
  "Greenest Transit Agency||Lowest CO2 per passenger mile",
  paste0(greenest[["Agency Name"]], "||", greenest$state, " · ", greenest$size),
  paste0(round(greenest$co2_lbs_per_mile, 2), "||lbs CO2 per passenger mile"),
  paste0("Typical agency: ", round(median_per_mile_all, 2)),
  paste0(fmt_ratio(greenest_times), " cleaner"),
  "best",

  "🏆",
  "Most Emissions Avoided||vs. everyone driving (CAFE)",
  paste0(winner_avoided[["Agency Name"]], "||", winner_avoided$state, " · ", winner_avoided$size),
  paste0(fmt_big(winner_avoided$avoided_tons), "||metric tons of CO2 avoided"),
  paste0(fmt_num(sum(avoided$avoided_tons > 0)), " of ", fmt_num(nrow(avoided)), " agencies avoid CO2"),
  paste0("Driving: ", fmt_ratio(winner_avoided$car_vs_transit), " more CO2"),
  "best",

  "🏆",
  "Clean Grid Champion||CO2 saved by a clean grid",
  paste0(champion[["Agency Name"]], "||", champion$state, " · ", champion_size),
  paste0(fmt_big(champion$grid_saving_tons), "||metric tons of CO2 saved"),
  paste0("Typical electric agency: ", fmt_big(median_saving)),
  paste0("Grid ", fmt_ratio(champion_grid_ratio), " cleaner"),
  "best",

  "🤦",
  "Missed Opportunity||Fuel only, in a clean-grid state",
  paste0(missed[["Agency Name"]], "||", missed$state, " · ", missed$size),
  paste0(round(missed$co2_lbs_per_mile, 2), "||lbs CO2 per passenger mile"),
  paste0(missed$size, " median: ", round(missed_median, 2)),
  paste0(fmt_ratio(missed_times), " the median"),
  "worst"
)

# Table
winners_tbl |>
  gt() |>
  # Best-of rows: green; worst-of row: grey
  text_transform(locations = cells_body(columns = award,  rows = type == "best"),  fn = stack_cell("14px", "#2E5E3A")) |>
  text_transform(locations = cells_body(columns = award,  rows = type == "worst"), fn = stack_cell("14px", "#6B6B6B")) |>
  text_transform(locations = cells_body(columns = winner),                          fn = stack_cell("13px", "#333333")) |>
  text_transform(locations = cells_body(columns = result, rows = type == "best"),  fn = stack_cell("22px", "#2E5E3A")) |>
  text_transform(locations = cells_body(columns = result, rows = type == "worst"), fn = stack_cell("22px", "#6B6B6B")) |>
  text_transform(locations = cells_body(columns = advantage, rows = type == "best"),  fn = pill("#E8F0E3", "#2E5E3A")) |>
  text_transform(locations = cells_body(columns = advantage, rows = type == "worst"), fn = pill("#E5E5E5", "#6B6B6B")) |>
  tab_style(style = cell_text(size = px(28)), locations = cells_body(columns = icon)) |>
  tab_style(style = cell_text(size = px(12), color = "#6B6B6B"), locations = cells_body(columns = reference)) |>
  tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#F2F2F2"), locations = cells_body(rows = type == "worst")) |>
  cols_align(align = "center", columns = c(icon, result, advantage)) |>
  cols_label(icon = "", award = "Award", winner = "Winner", result = "Result",
             reference = "Compared to", advantage = "") |>
  cols_hide(type) |>
  cols_width(
    icon      ~ px(40),
    award     ~ px(160),
    winner    ~ px(130),
    result    ~ px(130),
    reference ~ px(115),
    advantage ~ px(135)
  ) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "And the Winners Are…"
  ) |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(12), data_row.padding = px(6), table.width = pct(100)) |>
  tab_source_note("CAFE = 49 mpg fleet average for model year 2026 (NHTSA, 2022). Metric tons = lbs / 2,204.62") |>
  tab_source_note("Source: NTD 2025 (Energy Consumption, Service by Agency); U.S. EIA State Electricity Profiles") |>
  gta_theme()
```

Finally, we found them:

1. **Greenest Transit Agency** - **`r greenest[["Agency Name"]]`** in **`r greenest$state`**. We find **`r round(greenest$co2_lbs_per_mile, 2)`** lbs CO2 per passenger mile, compared to the typical agency's **`r round(median_per_mile_all, 2)`**. This winner is **`r fmt_ratio(greenest_times)`** cleaner.
2. **Most Emissions Avoided** - **`r winner_avoided[["Agency Name"]]`**. We find **`r fmt_big(winner_avoided$avoided_tons)`** metric tons of CO2 avoided. We note that driving would emit **`r fmt_ratio(winner_avoided$car_vs_transit)`** more CO2. For this award, we use the CAFE standard (NHTSA, 2022) - a new car (**`r cafe_mpg`** mpg) emits **`r round(car_per_mile, 2)`** lbs CO2 per mile. It's important to highlight that only **`r n_avoid`** of **`r n_avoided_all`** agencies avoid CO2, and **`r n_negative`** agencies emit more than if riders had driven. However, the CAFE standard evaluates against new cars, whereas a large number of older models are still running, and have much higher emissions. This limitation thus makes it more difficult to say if using transit would emit less than driving old cars.
3. **Clean Grid Champion** - **`r champion[["Agency Name"]]`** in **`r champion$state`**. We find **`r fmt_big(champion$grid_saving_tons)`** metric tons of CO2 saved. Its grid emits **`r fmt_num(champion$CO2_MWh)`** lbs/MWh vs. the U.S. average of **`r fmt_num(co2_us_weighted)`** (**`r fmt_ratio(champion_grid_ratio)`** cleaner). Furthermore, **`r fmt_big(median_saving)`** tons are saved by the typical agency using electricity. Perhaps it's time to move to New York?
4. **Missed Opportunity** - well, well, well... **`r missed[["Agency Name"]]`** (in **`r missed$state`**, in the **`r missed$size`** group) what happened there? In California, really? We had higher hopes for you in this ranking. We look at **`r round(missed$co2_lbs_per_mile, 2)`** lbs CO2 per passenger mile compared to your group's median of **`r round(missed_median, 2)`** (**`r fmt_ratio(missed_times)`** the median)... Additionally, we check for the state grid's quality, and find **`r fmt_num(missed$CO2_MWh)`** lbs/MWh, which is **`r fmt_ratio(missed_grid_ratio)`** cleaner than the U.S. average. Is there anything else to add? Perhaps that the **`r missed[["Agency Name"]]`** should consider electrifying.

**Note:** **`r winner_avoided[["Agency Name"]]`** wins two awards. Even if the grid is not the cleanest in the country, its size wins because a large portion of operations relies on electricity.

### 8/ Conclusion

Analyzing CO2 emissions across a system is tedious work. It requires the exploration, joining and comparison of several sources, plus additional calculations. It's very insightful work: crossing federal sources with many additional layers (from peers, or common practice guidance) to create a data set that can help answer quantitative and qualitative questions. We have analyzed different aspects: energy source per state, energy consumption and the whole U.S. transit-focused data. 

This allowed us to establish, step by step, a ranking of CO2 emissions by U.S. transit agencies. Main findings include:

1. An energy mix composed of electricity and fuels (with diesel in first position) dominates agency consumption across the country to power public transit.
2. The grid that powers the electricity consumed by an agency matters - if agencies use electricity produced by a dirty grid, their emissions rise.
3. The largest agencies, like NYC Transit, are the busiest, given the number of trips for some of the busiest cities in the country. Thus, total emissions follow the size of the agency (bigger agencies emit more CO2).
4. Converting different energy sources to a single metric allowed us to find the associated CO2 emissions per agency.
5. Given the high variability in city/agency/operations sizes, normalizing sizes by grouping agencies in 3 different buckets proved to be valuable, to easily compare agencies with similar sizes. We find that larger agencies are cleaner per passenger mile.
6. Winners have been defined using curated metrics, with the City of Seattle (Greenest Transit Agency), MTA NYC Transit (2 times winner with Most Emissions Avoided and Clean Grid Champion) and a big flop with the City of Glendale (Missed Opportunity, an agency whose fleet relies only on fuel, in a clean-grid state).
7. Overall, only **`r n_avoid`** of **`r n_avoided_all`** agencies beat a new **`r cafe_mpg`** mpg car.

We note some limitations, such as assumptions (e.g. B20, CAFE), and some agencies/states contain missing values or are under-reported. This can potentially bias some of the results, although we get a sense of the emissions of public transit across the U.S. Suggested next steps could include comparing results with real U.S. fleet fuel economy instead of CAFE, or comparing trends across years with APTA reports as consistency checks (to see an evolution, assess the effect of electrification, reduction in CO2 targets etc.).

This analysis once again proved how valuable it is to analyze performance based on real data, to understand how several sources can associate together to ultimately enrich and compare the data.

```{r}
#| label: t8-chart-avoided-emissions

# Top 5 agencies by CO2 avoided: CO2 if riders had driven vs. actual transit CO2

p_avoided <- ggplot(top_avoided, aes(y = reorder(name, avoided_tons))) +

                               "Source: NTD 2025 (Energy Consumption, Service by Agency); U.S. EIA State Electricity Profiles"), 110)
  ) +
  ggplot_theme_gta() +
  theme(
    plot.title            = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold", color = gta_green),
    plot.subtitle         = element_text(size = 10.5, color = gta_brown),
```

```{r}
#| label: t8-chart-missed

# All agencies in the Missed Opportunity's size group, CO2 per passenger mile,

missed_peers <- agency_norm |>
  filter(size == missed$size, !is.na(co2_lbs_per_mile)) |>
  left_join(select(EIA_SEP_REPORT, abbreviation, CO2_MWh), join_by(state == abbreviation)) |>
  mutate(

                 if_else(eligible, "Eligible: fuel only, clean-grid state", "Not eligible"))
  )

# Group sizes (eligible = used in the text)
n_eligible_medium <- sum(missed_peers$eligible)
n_other_medium    <- sum(!missed_peers$eligible)

# Legend labels, with counts
lab_eligible <- paste0("Eligible: fuel only, clean-grid state (", n_eligible_medium, ")")
lab_other    <- paste0("Other ", tolower(missed$size), " agencies (", n_other_medium, ")")

missed_peers <- missed_peers |>
  mutate(group = factor(if_else(eligible, lab_eligible, lab_other),
                        levels = c(lab_eligible, lab_other)))

# Plotting time

  # Median of the whole size group
  geom_vline(xintercept = missed_median, linetype = "dashed", color = gta_green, linewidth = 0.7) +
  annotate("text", x = missed_median, y = -0.55, hjust = -0.05, size = 3.4,

                         position = position_jitter(height = 0.35, width = 0, seed = 42),

  geom_point_interactive(data = filter(missed_peers, eligible, !is_missed),
                         aes(tooltip = tip, data_id = `NTD ID`, color = group),
                         position = position_jitter(height = 0.35, width = 0, seed = 7),
                         alpha = 0.85, size = 2.6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = setNames(c(gta_brown, "#C9C4B9"), c(lab_eligible, lab_other)),
                      breaks = c(lab_eligible, lab_other), name = NULL) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1))) +
  # 3. On top: the Missed Opportunity (red dot) + label
  geom_point_interactive(data = filter(missed_peers, is_missed),

  scale_x_log10(labels = label_number(accuracy = 0.01),

    plot.title.position   = "plot",
    plot.caption.position = "plot",
    legend.text           = element_text(size = 9.5),
    axis.text             = element_text(size = 9.5),
    panel.grid.major.y    = element_blank(),
```

*The Green Transit Alliance* is happy to present this year's most awaited winners of the GTA Green Transit Awards. We applaud the **`r greenest[["Agency Name"]]`** (**`r greenest$state`**) as the greenest agency, and **`r winner_avoided[["Agency Name"]]`** (**`r winner_avoided$state`**), which wins both the most emissions avoided and clean grid champion awards. We, however, shame **`r missed[["Agency Name"]]`** (**`r missed$state`**) for the biggest missed opportunity (misses a chance to be great, but still wins an award).
:::

**New York, NY - November 6, 2026 -** Dear readers, this year has been particularly interesting. For the first time, we enriched our Data & Analytics capabilities by cross-referencing valuable sources for the awards. Our team went above and beyond the expected process by including not only the overall energy consumption NTD data source, but also the EIA State Electricity Profiles to add a layer to combine with our NTD Service report. 

This allowed the GTA to publish this highly curated report that details: how much energy each agency consumes (NTD Energy), how much transit a given agency delivers and where (NTD Service) and, finally, how clean the electricity produced in each state is (EIA). As transit electrification grew, we wanted to take a closer look at the electricity produced, since it can only be as clean as the grid that powers it. We hope, with this granularity, to give more insights into the U.S. landscape and keep expanding our capabilities to cover larger areas in the world each year. 

Take a look at the detailed results below, and we're happy to receive any feedback to improve our activities.

::: {style="border-left: 5px solid #A7C957; background-color: rgba(255,255,255,0.08); padding: 1em 1.5em; margin: 1.5em 0; border-radius: 4px;"}
#### 🏆 Greenest Transit Agency

::: {.pr-stats}
::: {.pr-stat}
[`r round(greenest$co2_lbs_per_mile, 2)`]{.pr-num} [lbs CO2 per passenger mile]{.pr-lbl}
:::
::: {.pr-stat}
[`r fmt_ratio(greenest_times)`]{.pr-num} [cleaner than the typical agency]{.pr-lbl}
:::
:::

To calculate the greenest agency, we measured CO2 emissions per passenger mile (simply put, a passenger mile is one person traveling one mile). **`r greenest[["Agency Name"]]`** (**`r greenest$state`**) wins, with **`r round(greenest$co2_lbs_per_mile, 2)`** lbs per passenger mile. 

As a comparison, the typical agency emits **`r round(median_per_mile_all, 2)`** lbs per passenger mile, which makes **`r greenest[["Agency Name"]]`** **`r fmt_ratio(greenest_times)`** cleaner.
:::

::: {style="border-left: 5px solid #A7C957; background-color: rgba(255,255,255,0.08); padding: 1em 1.5em; margin: 1.5em 0; border-radius: 4px;"}
#### 🏆 Most Emissions Avoided

::: {.pr-stats}
::: {.pr-stat}
[`r fmt_big(winner_avoided$avoided_tons)`]{.pr-num} [metric tons of CO2 avoided]{.pr-lbl}
:::
::: {.pr-stat}
[`r fmt_ratio(winner_avoided$car_vs_transit)`]{.pr-num} [more CO2 if riders drove]{.pr-lbl}
:::
:::

For this particular award, we used industry assumptions (CAFE standard, **`r cafe_mpg`** mpg, one person per car) to compare CO2 emissions in this report with CO2 emissions if transit riders had driven new cars. We subtract the actual CO2 emissions from the CO2 from driving (assumed).

The agency that managed to avoid the most emissions is **`r winner_avoided[["Agency Name"]]`**, with **`r fmt_big(winner_avoided$avoided_tons)`** metric tons avoided. As a comparison, driving would emit **`r fmt_ratio(winner_avoided$car_vs_transit)`** more CO2. We also note that only **`r n_avoid`** of **`r n_avoided_all`** agencies avoid CO2 at all (against new cars only, which is a strong limitation since a lot of older, less fuel-efficient cars are still running in the country).


```{r}
#| label: pr-chart-avoided
#| echo: false
chart_avoided
```

:::

::: {style="border-left: 5px solid #A7C957; background-color: rgba(255,255,255,0.08); padding: 1em 1.5em; margin: 1.5em 0; border-radius: 4px;"}
#### 🏆 Clean Grid Champion

::: {.pr-stats}
::: {.pr-stat}
[`r fmt_big(champion$grid_saving_tons)`]{.pr-num} [metric tons of CO2 saved]{.pr-lbl}
:::
::: {.pr-stat}
[`r fmt_ratio(champion_grid_ratio)`]{.pr-num} [cleaner grid than the U.S. average]{.pr-lbl}
:::
:::

As transit electrification intensifies, we wanted to assess which agency's operations save the most CO2 emissions. We multiplied the electricity used by the agency by how much cleaner the state grid is than the U.S. average.

We found our champion with the most CO2 saved: **`r champion[["Agency Name"]]`** with **`r fmt_big(champion$grid_saving_tons)`** tons saved. Its grid is **`r fmt_ratio(champion_grid_ratio)`** cleaner than average. For reference, a typical electric agency saves **`r fmt_big(median_saving)`** tons of CO2, which favorably places our champion.
:::

::: {style="border-left: 5px solid #8C8C8C; background-color: rgba(0,0,0,0.20); padding: 1em 1.5em; margin: 1.5em 0; border-radius: 4px;"}
#### 🤦 Missed Opportunity

::: {.pr-stats .pr-worst}
::: {.pr-stat}
[`r round(missed$co2_lbs_per_mile, 2)`]{.pr-num} [lbs CO2 per passenger mile]{.pr-lbl}
:::
::: {.pr-stat}
[`r fmt_ratio(missed_times)`]{.pr-num} [its size group's median]{.pr-lbl}
:::
:::

Fair game; we had to find the "worst-of" this year. What if we told you that an agency relies solely on fuel when its state has a cleaner-than-average grid? That's what we verified by selecting the highest CO2 per passenger mile, among the fuel-only agencies operating in clean-grid states.

That's the case for **`r missed[["Agency Name"]]`** in **`r missed$state`**, with **`r round(missed$co2_lbs_per_mile, 2)`** lbs per passenger mile. To put it in perspective, this represents **`r fmt_ratio(missed_times)`** its group median (**`r round(missed_median, 2)`**), in a state whose grid is **`r fmt_ratio(missed_grid_ratio)`** cleaner than average. Worst of all, on top of being the worst among the **`r n_eligible_medium`** fuel-only **`r missed$size`** agencies in clean-grid states, it's also the worst across all **`r missed$size`** agencies... We expect some improvement for next year, **`r missed[["Agency Name"]]`**!

```{r}
chart_missed
```

**About the Green Transit Alliance**

No, we are not the popular video game Grand Theft Auto (same acronym, completely different world). We're an organization dedicated to developing green energy across transit systems in the U.S. We're also dedicated to doing research to surface areas of improvement, where agencies can improve their operations to make the country a better place to live. We have extensive experience in stakeholder management, data and analytics and are known for our annual GTA Green Transit Awards, which reward the best players and flag those most in need of improvement.

P.S.: please refrain from sending us inquiries about when the video game will finally come out (look at the logo please, it's a green leaf, not a gangster).
